records.researcher_notes:
This card proposes a new plant that GEM does not list, with two engine units. Check the engine counts and sizes against the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality application below. The point is approximate until it is checked on a map.

Where to find it:
- Open https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/ASCsZfZJOr8EbvF%C3%81Ggb4d5pgBB8P%C3%893SavzfBq06GG90H9bIu884yqy5xtHsV9LFXKJVMOhq8Jt7BeOnZ7nXm4%C3%89E%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true (an air quality permit application dated September 2026 from Rose Rock Environmental Services for 6000 N Shartel Ave, LLC, facility OKC2).
- Page 1 of the PDF, cover letter: the application is for "an additional eight (8) natural gas-fired, four-stroke lean burn" engines. "Six (6) of these engines would be operating and two (2) would be available for back-up power". They are added to "the original permitted 11 4SLB SI RICE engines" under permit 2026-0216-C "issued on August 26, 2026".
- Page 4 of the PDF, printed page 1 of 40, "Project Scope and Description": the 11-engine permit is for engines "to provide continuous onsite power".
- Page 5 of the PDF, "Process Description": the plant "operates exclusively in island mode" and so is "completely independent of the external utility grid". It will have "up to nineteen (19)" engines.

Engines and capacity:
- Page 13 of the PDF, engine data sheet: Wartsila 20V34SG, quantity (16), "Electrical Output (kWe) 9,000".
- Page 14 of the PDF, engine data sheet: Wartsila 18V34SG, quantity (3), "Electrical Output (kWe) 5,940".
- The total is 16 times 9.0 MW plus 3 times 5.94 MW, which is 161.82 MW. I added this up myself. The application does not print a plant total.
- Page 5 says some engines in each group are designated as backup within the fleet. Page 12, note 2 to the emissions table, says "Will not operate more than 14 engines at any time." The full 19 engines are still the installed capacity.

Start-up and owner:
- Page 26 of the PDF, general facility information form: "Est. Date of Construction/Modification Start: 1Q2027" and "Operational Start-up: 1Q2027". So none of the engines can be running yet.
- Page 6 of the PDF, "Emission Sources" table, gives construction dates of 2026 for some engines and the first quarter of 2027 for others.
- Page 26, section 1 "Company Information": the applicant is "6000 N Shartel Ave, LLC". Page 13 headers also say "Scale Datacenter". The owner is the permit holder, and no match exists in the entity list.

Location:
- Page 26 of the PDF, section 8 "Geographic Coordinates": "Latitude (to 5 Decimals) 35.53351" and "Longitude (to 5 Decimals) -97.52242". The same page gives the address as 6000 N Shartel Ave and the county as Oklahoma.
- This is the applicant's point on a form, not a point seen on a map, so the location stays approximate.

Why this differs:
- Unit 1 as the 16 Wartsila 20V34SG engines and unit 2 as the three 18V34SG engines is my grouping. The application lists the engines one by one as ENG1 to ENG19 on page 6.

records.researcher_notes: GEM does not list this plant. The Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality permit evaluation of November 5, 2025 covers Myall, LLC and its PRY Data Storage Facility in Pryor, Mayes County, at 36.2425 north and 95.3302 west. The facility has emergency generator engines, some fitted with selective catalytic reduction, plus fire pump engines. Myall asked the department to keep all engine details confidential, so the engine count and size are not public. The nitrogen oxide limit in the permit is 249 tons a year, which is a large fleet but gives no megawatt figure. Myall LLC is the company that bought the land for Google's Pryor campus in the MidAmerica Industrial Park, so this is very likely a Google building. The permit itself does not name Google. The record is added with capacity blank, as the rules say for an unknown size. Diesel is the fuel named for the generators in the permit, and the permit also says the facility burns natural gas in other equipment. Unit 1 is the emergency generator engine group.

This card proposes one new plant in Coal County with three engine groups. The groups are grouped because each site is under 50 MW alone and together they are 61.7 MW. Check the three sites and engine counts below, and note that the owner needs a new entity.

Where to find it:
- Open https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/Aevth4xmYyMYEUksZxJwUqGnaRaWfTbuqstqjNNkWYX43sTZcmwOpZkwiQnIvBom5aPYVRnVFqOmoareNhLZSGg%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true (a chain of emails between the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality and the cooperative's consultant, filed in August 2026).
- Page 1 of the PDF, the department's cover email of August 10, 2026, lists three applications. Targa is facility 17249, permit 2025-0677-C. Little Dixie is facility 18772, permit 2025-0678-C. Centrahoma is facility 17248, permit 2025-0679-C. All three show "Initial application received October 30, 2024" and "Tier II construction application received August 18, 2025".
- The email chain on pages 2 to 8 shows the department still asking questions on all three applications as of August 7, 2026, so the applications are still in review.
- Open https://okdeqonbaseexternal.databankcloud.com/pav/api/Document/Adi%C3%81Uj4HU48j7TJinfPrZ7F99J8r2OmzRMCr78Mar5%C3%81iTb6ZjN92Z8hh1DZPsPqO7bKF3FxOM26IVudy91ABEfs%3D/?ViewerMode=PDF&ForceDownload=true (a May 6, 2026 email and revised pages for the Little Dixie application).
- Page 1 of the PDF: "we are needing to incorporate two new generator engines into the permit application."

Engine counts:
- Page 3 of that second PDF, "Attachment 3 Updated Facility-Wide Potential Emissions Summary, Little Dixie Facility": five rows, "Caterpillar G3520H TA Generator Engine (3448 Hp)", GEN1 to GEN5.
- Pages 9 and 10 of that second PDF, "Attachment 4" tables 6 and 7: "Caterpillar G3520K Generator Engine" GEN6 and GEN7, 3513 horsepower each. These are the two newer engines.
- I could not find the counts of ten engines at Targa and ten at Centrahoma in either linked file. They come from my earlier reading of the state permit files.
- I also could not find the per-engine figure of 2.469 MW or the planned spring 2027 date in either file. The first email chain talks only about emission factors.

Other sources:
- Open https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx (the Energy Information Administration monthly generator inventory, September 2026), sheet "Operating". Entity Name "Peoples Electric Cooperative", County "Coal", Technology "Natural Gas Internal Combustion Engine", Status "(OP) Operating".
- Plant ID 68376 "Centrahoma East" has ten generators, IDs 142 to 145, 149, 150 and 155 to 158. Plant ID 68377 "Centrahoma West" has ten, IDs 151 to 154, 161, 164 to 168. Plant ID 68378 "Little Dixie" has five, IDs 146 to 148, 159 and 160.
- Each generator shows "Nameplate Capacity (MW)" 2.5, "Operating Month" July and "Operating Year" 2019.
- The same sheet lists two smaller Peoples plants. Buzzard Flop, plant 68375, in Hughes County has three generators of 2.5 MW (7.5 MW). Stuart (OK), plant 68379, in Pittsburg County has two of 2.5 MW (5 MW). Each is under 50 MW alone and is not added.
- The Southwest Power Pool active request list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive: row ASGI-2016-012, nearest town "Centrahoma", capacity 61.725 MW, status "IA FULLY EXECUTED/COMMERCIAL OPERATION". This is one entry that matches the three sites together.

Why this differs:
- The Energy Information Administration calls the sites Centrahoma East, Centrahoma West and Little Dixie. The state permit files call them Targa, Centrahoma and Little Dixie. I could not match East and West to Targa and Centrahoma from these files.
- The Energy Information Administration lists each engine at 2.5 MW. The 2.469 MW figure is a more exact rating from my earlier reading.

Owner:
- The entity lookup found no entity for any spelling of Peoples Electric Cooperative, so a new entity is needed. I did not repeat that lookup.

records.researcher_notes:
This card proposes a new project that GEM does not list, from one row of the Southwest Power Pool surplus interconnection list. Check the row below. The engine details are not on that page, so they rest on the study I read earlier. Status is pre-construction because the interconnection agreement is "IA FULLY EXECUTED/ON SCHEDULE".

Where to find it:
- Open https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive (the Southwest Power Pool "Generator Interconnection Active Request Listing", heading "GI Active Requests", one large table).
- Find the row where "Generation Interconnection Number" is GEN-2025-SR19. The study group column says "Surplus".
- "Nearest Town or County" is Chouteau, "State" is OK and "TO at POI" (the transmission owner) is GRDA.
- "Capacity (MW)" is 100, "Service Type" is ER, "Generation Type" is Thermal, and "Fuel Type" is blank.
- "Substation or Line" is "Maid 161kV substation".
- "Commercial Operation Date" is November 30, 2029. "Request Received" is June 12, 2025.
- "Status" is "IA FULLY EXECUTED/ON SCHEDULE".

What the page does not show:
- "Nameplate Capacity" and "Requested Maximum Injection Capability (MW)" are both 0 on this row, and the "Associated Studies" cell is empty. So the page does not give the engine make or count.
- The earlier note says the study describes 31 Cummins C3250 D6e diesel engines totaling 100.76 MW in the study table, with injection capped at 100 MW. Each engine is 4.063 megavolt-amperes, which is 3.25 MW at the usual power factor. I could not reopen the study, so this comes from my earlier reading.

Other sources:
- The study says the engines use spare capacity at the point where GEN-2019-002 already connects. On the same page, GEN-2019-002 is a "Battery/Storage" request in Mayes, with GRDA as transmission owner, capacity 100 MW and commercial operation November 30, 2027.
- The battery row on the page shows 100 MW. The earlier note gave 101.5 MW, which came from the study and not from this page. I could not reopen the study.

Not found:
- SPP does not publish the company behind a request, and the table has no owner column. I found no regulator filing or news item naming one, so the owner is blank.
- The page gives only the substation, so no coordinates are proposed.
- Whether these are backup engines for a data center or a stand-alone peaking plant is not stated in the study.

verifications.note: Row for Georgia-Pacific Muskogee, plant 10362, Muskogee County: GEN1 25 MW, GEN2 44.5 MW and GEN3 44.5 MW natural gas steam turbines, operating since 1979, 1980 and 1982.

Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality notice from January 2016 for the Georgia-Pacific Muskogee mill at Chandler Road, describing power boilers that co-generate electricity through steam turbines.
Map link to the plant point from the federal file; it falls on the mill site in Muskogee.

records.researcher_notes:
This card proposes a new plant with three units, a captive power plant at a paper mill. Check the three turbines in the federal file below. Read the linked question card about GEM's Fort James plant first, because these may be the same turbines.

Where to find it:
- Open https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx (the Energy Information Administration monthly generator inventory, titled "Inventory of Operating Generators as of September 2026"), sheet "Operating".
- Find "Plant ID" 10362, "Plant Name" "Georgia-Pacific Muskogee", "County" Muskogee, "Plant State" OK.
- Generator GEN1: "Technology" "Natural Gas Steam Turbine", "Nameplate Capacity (MW)" 25, "Operating Year" 1979, "Operating Month" June.
- Generator GEN2: same technology, 44.5 MW, June 1980.
- Generator GEN3: same technology, 44.5 MW, November 1982.
- All three show "Status" "(OP) Operating" and "Sector" "Industrial CHP". The total is 114 MW.
- The same rows give "Latitude" 35.7322 and "Longitude" -95.2939. Open https://www.google.com/maps?q=35.7322,-95.2939 to see that point as a pin. A pin from a federal file is not a point checked on the ground, so the location stays approximate.

Owner and mill:
- In the federal file, "Entity Name" is "Georgia-Pacific Muskogee LLC". The card uses Georgia-Pacific LLC, which already exists as an entity.
- Open https://applications.deq.ok.gov/permitspublic/storedpermits/3131.pdf (an Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality permit memorandum dated January 27, 2016, marked "DRAFT/PROPOSED"). Page 1 of the PDF names "Georgia-Pacific Consumer Products LP", "Muskogee Mill", "Facility ID No.: 643", "4901 Chandler Road, Muskogee". It says the company "owns and operates a recycle deinking paper mill".
- Page 2 of the PDF, "Background and Scope of Modification": "The common steam header provides steam to both process units and electric-generating steam turbines. The steam turbines use the steam to produce electricity for use on-site". The memo is about replacing a coal boiler with a gas boiler. It gives no turbine sizes.

Why this differs:
- The permit memo names the company as Georgia-Pacific Consumer Products LP, and the federal file names Georgia-Pacific Muskogee LLC. Neither says Georgia-Pacific LLC. The card uses the parent company name.
- The memo gives the point as 35.73589 north and 95.30489 west on page 1. That is about 1 kilometer from the federal file point. I used the federal point.

Not found:
- No document shows the units retired. The "Retired" sheet of the federal file has no Georgia-Pacific Muskogee or Fort James entry.
- GEM already lists a Fort James Muskogee Mill power plant with two coal units of 45.5 MW marked retired in 2020, with a note about conversion to gas. I did not reopen GEM for this. The link between the two is the open question on the linked card.
